title: Stop Syncing Folders: Why SharePoint Shortcuts Are Breaking Your Enterprise Data Strategy

entities.name: Mirko Peters
entities.quote: Follow me, Mirko Peters, on LinkedIn for more structural clarity.

entities.name: Sensitivity labels
entities.quote: Windows File Explorer doesn't understand sensitivity labels in the same way the browser does.

entities.name: Zero Trust
entities.quote: it is a fundamental betrayal of the zero trust philosophy.

entities.name: Conditional Access
entities.quote: They don't need to bypass your complex conditional access policies

entities.name: Data loss prevention (DLP)
entities.quote: It can't apply real-time data loss prevention.

entities.name: SharePoint
entities.quote: We tell users they are connecting to SharePoint.

entities.name: OneDrive
entities.quote: But the one drive sync client operates on a much cruder level.

entities.name: Microsoft Teams
entities.quote: We need to train our people to use teams as their primary interface for collaboration

quotes.text: We are still trying to pretend that a SharePoint document library is just a Z-drive with a fancy web interface. It isn't. It is a sophisticated content service.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes SharePoint as a content service rather than a network drive, the core argument against syncing.

quotes.text: Because that folder is a shortcut to a shared SharePoint library, the command propagates instantly. They aren't just deleting a link. They are wiping the actual files from the source for every single person in the company.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the concrete deletion-cascade risk of OneDrive shortcuts.

quotes.text: If your governance doesn't explicitly block the use of the one-drive client on unmanaged or non-compliant devices, you have a massive hole in your perimeter.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, actionable security recommendation for unmanaged devices.

quotes.text: Most organizations don't even realize they are hitting this wall because they think in terms of gigabytes, not item counts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains a common blind spot behind sync performance failures.

quotes.text: If you hide the sync button, without changing the culture, your users will find a way around it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Stresses that adoption and culture matter more than technical lockdown.

takeaways: Syncing SharePoint libraries replicates data onto endpoints, stripping metadata, versioning context and real-time protections like DLP and sensitivity labels.
OneDrive shortcuts avoid per-device replication but introduce deletion cascades and an admin visibility gap that require new governance and user training.
Large libraries beyond roughly 300,000 items break the sync model, so organizations should favor browser, Teams and Office app access enforced through Intune and sensitivity labels.
hook: Every click on the OneDrive sync button copies enterprise data onto endpoints and away from the controls that protect it. This episode is for Microsoft 365 architects and IT admins who want to understand why syncing and shortcuts fragment their SharePoint data strategy. You will learn the security, metadata and scale limits of sync and how to move teams to cloud-native access.
